def-locally-finite-homotopy-type:
## Definition

A homotopy type $X$ is **locally finite** if every homotopy group $\pi_i(X,x)$ is finite for every point $x$, and for each $x$ there is an integer $n_x$ such that $\pi_i(X,x)=0$ for $i>n_x$.

Write $\pi_0(X)$ for the set of connected components. Let $\mathbb Q_c(X)$ be the rational-valued functions on $\pi_0(X)$ with finite support. For a component $x$, the **homotopy weight** is
$$
w_X(x):=\prod_{i>0}|\pi_i(X,x)|^{(-1)^i}.
$$
The product is finite because the positive homotopy groups vanish in high degrees; a negative exponent means a reciprocal.

For a map $f:X\to Y$ of locally finite homotopy types and $\alpha\in\mathbb Q_c(X)$, define
$$
f_!(\alpha)(y):=\sum_{x\in\pi_0(F_y)}\alpha(i_y(x))\,w_{F_y}(x),
$$
where $F_y$ is the homotopy fiber of $f$ at $y$ ([[def-homotopy-fiber-of-a-map]]) and $i_y:F_y\to X$ is its natural map. For a proper map, meaning one whose homotopy fibers have finitely many connected components, also define $f^*:\mathbb Q_c(Y)\to\mathbb Q_c(X)$ by $f^*\beta=\beta\circ\pi_0(f)$.

The ratio lemma [[lem-homotopy-fiber-component-weight-ratio]] proves that fibers of maps between locally finite homotopy types are locally finite and that the displayed sum is finite. The set of components of a homotopy fiber alone does not determine $f_!$.
lem-homotopy-cardinality-base-change:
## Statement

Let a homotopy-cartesian square of locally finite homotopy types be given, with its lower map $u$ proper on components. Then the upper map $u'$ is proper on components and $u^*\circ f_!=(f')_!\circ(u')^*$ on finite-support functions. The square's maps are displayed after the proof.
lem-homotopy-fiber-component-weight-rati:
## Statement

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of locally finite homotopy types, let $y\in\pi_0(Y)$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb Q_c(X)$. For each component $x\in\pi_0(X)$ mapping to $y$, put
$$
r_f(x,y):=\prod_{j>0}|\pi_j(X,x)|^{(-1)^j}|\pi_j(Y,y)|^{(-1)^{j+1}}.
$$
Then the total homotopy weight of the components of the fiber over $y$ that map to $x$ is $r_f(x,y)$. Consequently,
$$
f_!(\alpha)(y)=\sum_{\substack{x\in\pi_0(X)\\f(x)=y}}\alpha(x)r_f(x,y).
$$
In particular, every homotopy fiber is locally finite and the defining sum for $f_!$ is finite.
def-toen-locally-finite-dg-category:
## Definition

Fix a finite field $k=\mathbb F_q$ ([[def-finite-field-and-its-order]]). A **small $k$-linear dg-category** $\mathcal T$ has a set of objects, a cochain complex $\mathcal T(a,b)$ of $k$-vector spaces for every ordered pair, closed degree-zero identity maps, and associative degree-zero composition chain maps
$$
\mathcal T(b,c)\otimes_k\mathcal T(a,b)\longrightarrow\mathcal T(a,c).
$$
The cohomological grading and differential follow [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]. Each endomorphism complex is a differential graded algebra in the sense of [[def-differential-graded-algebra]].

The dg-category is **locally finite** when, for every $a,b$, the graded vector space $\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}H^i(\mathcal T(a,b))$ is finite-dimensional. Thus the cohomology is finite-dimensional and vanishes outside a finite set of degrees; no uniform bound over all pairs is assumed.

A **right dg $\mathcal T$-module** is a dg-functor $\mathcal T^{op}\to\mathrm{Ch}(k)$: it assigns a cochain complex $M(a)$ to each object and compatible degree-zero right composition actions. On each endomorphism algebra $\mathcal T(a,a)$ this is the right differential graded module structure of [[def-differential-graded-module]]. A quasi-isomorphism is a module map inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology group at every object.

The enhancement used here includes the standard projective model category of right dg modules ([[def-model-category-and-quillen-adjunction]]): its weak equivalences are the quasi-isomorphisms just defined, its fibrations are objectwise degreewise surjections, and its representable modules are homotopically projective, so their dg Hom complexes compute derived Hom. Its homotopy category $\mathcal D(\mathcal T)$ is triangulated. The same objectwise homotopy theory is used for arrow diagrams and composable-pair diagrams. It is stable: it is pointed, and a square is a homotopy pushout exactly when it is a homotopy pullback. The translation is the cohomological shift, and a homotopy cofiber of a module map is represented functorially by its mapping cone. These homotopy-theory structures are part of the supplied dg enhancement; an unenhanced triangulated category alone is not an input.

For modules $a,b$, write $\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal T}(a,b)$ for the derived Hom complex in the supplied projective homotopy theory. Its derived mapping space has $\pi_j\operatorname{Map}(a,b)=H^{-j}\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathcal T}(a,b)=\operatorname{Ext}^{-j}_{\mathcal T}(a,b)$ for $j\ge0$. In the core homotopy type of a category of modules, $\pi_1$ at $a$ is $\operatorname{Aut}(a)$ and $\pi_i=\operatorname{Ext}^{1-i}_{\mathcal T}(a,a)$ for $i>1$.

For $a\in\mathcal T$, the **representable right module** is $h_a=\mathcal T(-,a)$. A module is **perfect** if its object in $\mathcal D(\mathcal T)$ belongs to the smallest full triangulated subcategory containing all representables and closed under retracts. This means it is obtained from finitely many representables by finite direct sums, shifts, cones, and direct summands. For perfect modules set
$$
\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal T}(x,y):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D(\mathcal T)}(x,y[i]).
$$
lem-homotopy-cardinality-pushforward-is-:
## Statement

For maps $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ of locally finite homotopy types,
$$
(g\circ f)_!=g_!\circ f_!:\mathbb Q_c(X)\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_c(Z).
$$
def-toen-derived-hall-algebra:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally finite dg-enhancement over the finite field $\Bbbk=\mathbb F_q$ in the sense of [[def-toen-locally-finite-dg-category]]. Let $X^{(0)}$ be the core homotopy type of its perfect-module category: points are perfect modules, paths are quasi-isomorphisms, and higher paths are the derived mapping spaces. Let $X^{(1)}$ be the core homotopy type of arrows between perfect modules and $X^{(2)}$ the core homotopy type of composable pairs. These are the cores of the corresponding objectwise homotopy theories, so their equivalences are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms.

An arrow $u:x\to y$ determines three maps
$$
s(u)=x,\qquad c(u)=y,\qquad t(u)=\operatorname{Cone}(u),
$$
where $\operatorname{Cone}(u)$ is the functorial homotopy cofiber in the supplied dg enhancement. Thus $s\times t:X^{(1)}\to X^{(0)}\times X^{(0)}$ remembers the source and cofiber, and $c:X^{(1)}\to X^{(0)}$ remembers the target. For a composable pair $x\to y\to z$, write $f$ for the first arrow, $g$ for the second, $h$ for the composite, and $k:\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to\operatorname{Cone}(h)$ for the induced map of cofibers.

Set
$$
\mathcal{DH}(\mathcal T):=\mathbb Q_c(X^{(0)}).
$$
The product is the convolution
$$
\alpha*\beta:=c_!\big((s\times t)^*(\alpha\otimes\beta)\big),
$$
where $(\alpha\otimes\beta)(x,y)=\alpha(x)\beta(y)$ on $X^{(0)}\times X^{(0)}$, and $c_!$ and pullback are those of [[def-locally-finite-homotopy-type]]. For an isomorphism class $x$ of perfect modules, let $\chi_x$ be its characteristic function. The $\chi_x$ form a basis, and
$$
\chi_x*\chi_y=\sum_z g^z_{x,y}\chi_z,
$$
where $g^z_{x,y}$ is the weighted homotopy cardinality of the fiber of $c$ over $z$ restricted to arrows with source isomorphic to $x$ and cofiber isomorphic to $y$.

The zero module gives the candidate unit $\chi_0$. The definition is well-defined: local finiteness and finite support of the convolution follow from [[lem-derived-hall-moduli-spaces-and-convolution-are-finite]].
lem-perfect-dg-modules-have-finite-total:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally finite dg-category over $\mathbb F_q$ in the sense of [[def-toen-locally-finite-dg-category]]. For any two perfect right dg $\mathcal T$-modules $x,y$, the graded vector space
$$
\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal T}(x,y)
$$
is finite-dimensional. In particular, every Ext group is finite and all but finitely many vanish.
lem-derived-hall-moduli-spaces-and-convo:
## Statement

For a locally finite dg-enhancement $\mathcal T$, the moduli homotopy types $X^{(0)}$, $X^{(1)}$, and $X^{(2)}$ of [[def-toen-derived-hall-algebra]] are locally finite. The map $s\times t:X^{(1)}\to X^{(0)}\times X^{(0)}$ is proper on components. Consequently the pull-push expression defining $\mathcal{DH}(\mathcal T)$ is a well-defined product on finite-support functions.
lem-derived-hall-stabilizer-homotopy-seq:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally finite dg-enhancement over $k=\mathbb F_q$, let $x,z$ be perfect right dg $\mathcal T$-modules, and let $f:x\to z$ be a morphism whose homotopy cofiber is isomorphic to a perfect module $y$. Let $C_f$ be the connected component represented by $f$ in the homotopy fiber over $z$ of the target map from the arrow homotopy type, restricted to source isomorphic to $x$ and cofiber isomorphic to $y$. Put
$$
\operatorname{Aut}(f/z):=\{a\in\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal D(\mathcal T)}(x): f\circ a=f\text{ in }\mathcal D(\mathcal T)\}.
$$
Then
$$
\prod_{j>0}|\pi_j(C_f,f)|^{(-1)^j} =|\operatorname{Aut}(f/z)|^{-1} \prod_{i>0}|\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_{\mathcal T}(x,z)|^{(-1)^i} \prod_{i>0}|\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}_{\mathcal T}(x,x)|^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$
lem-derived-hall-associativity-squares:
## Statement

Let $X^{(0)},X^{(1)},X^{(2)}$ and $s,c,t,f,g,h,k$ be as in [[def-toen-derived-hall-algebra]]. The arrow-composition square (first diagram below) and the composite-cofiber square (second diagram below) are homotopy cartesian.
thm-toen-derived-hall-number-formula:
## Statement

Let $x,y,z$ be perfect right dg $\mathcal T$-modules for a locally finite dg-enhancement $\mathcal T$. Define
$$
[x,z]_y:=\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D(\mathcal T)}(x,z):\operatorname{Cone}(f)\cong y\}
$$
and let $\operatorname{Aut}(x)$ act on this finite set by precomposition. For $f\in[x,z]_y$, write
$$
\operatorname{Aut}(f/z):=\{a\in\operatorname{Aut}(x): f\circ a=f\}.
$$
Then the coefficient in [[def-toen-derived-hall-algebra]] is
$$
g^z_{x,y} = \sum_{[f]\in[x,z]_y/\operatorname{Aut}(x)} \frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}(f/z)|} \prod_{i>0}|\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}(x,z)|^{(-1)^i} |\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}(x,x)|^{(-1)^{i+1}}
$$
and equivalently
$$
g^z_{x,y} = \frac{|[x,z]_y|\displaystyle\prod_{i>0}|\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}(x,z)|^{(-1)^i}} {|\operatorname{Aut}(x)|\displaystyle\prod_{i>0}|\operatorname{Ext}^{-i}(x,x)|^{(-1)^i}}.
$$
All products are finite because perfect modules have finite total Ext.
thm-toen-derived-hall-algebra-is-associa:
## Statement

For every locally finite dg-enhancement $\mathcal T$ over a finite field, the convolution of [[def-toen-derived-hall-algebra]] is a well-defined associative $\mathbb Q$-algebra. Its unit is $\chi_0$, the characteristic function of the zero module.
thm-hereditary-heart-embeds-in-derived-h:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally finite dg-enhancement over $\mathbb F_q$, and let $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Perf}(\mathcal T)$. Suppose $\mathcal D$ has a bounded t-structure whose heart $\mathcal A$ is a small finitary hereditary abelian category, and suppose the inclusion induces an exact equivalence $D^b(\mathcal A)\simeq\mathcal D$ under which short exact sequences in $\mathcal A$ correspond to distinguished triangles with all three terms in the heart. Here **hereditary** means cohomological dimension at most one: $\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b(\mathcal A)}(M,N[i])=0$ for all $M,N\in\mathcal A$ and $i>1$.

The untwisted Hall product [[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]] uses the convention that $[M]*_{\mathcal A}[N]$ counts subobjects isomorphic to $N$ with quotient $M$. With this convention, the basis map
$$
\Phi:H_{\mathcal A,\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\mathcal{DH}(\mathcal T), \qquad [M]\longmapsto\chi_M
$$
is an injective algebra anti-homomorphism:
$$
\Phi([M]*_{\mathcal A}[N])=\Phi([N])*_{\mathcal{DH}}\Phi([M]).
$$
Equivalently, it is an algebra embedding $H_{\mathcal A,\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{DH}(\mathcal T)$. Its image is the subalgebra spanned by the characteristic functions of heart objects.
